# GARS execution environment — the single definition of how to run a skill.
#
# Source this from every submit.sh:  source "$WS/_system/gars-env.sh"
#
# Why this file exists: the same ~10 lines of setup were previously copy-pasted into every
# submit.sh, in every project, for every sub-stage. They drifted — a salvaged script was found
# still referencing a vendored skills path that no longer existed.
#
# Why absolute paths rather than `conda activate`: activation would work, but stacking two
# environments needs conda's shell hook sourced inside every batch script, which is more moving
# parts and fails differently on nodes where the hook is absent. Absolute paths behave
# identically everywhere, which is what a Slurm script needs.
#
# Why this lives in the workspace and not in $HOME: a workspace is a copy of the template and
# the contracts treat it as self-contained, so copying a workspace carries its environment
# definition. It is versioned in git, so a change is a reviewable commit rather than an
# untracked edit to a home-directory script.

# --- root ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DO NOT substitute $HOME here. On this cluster $HOME (/gpfs/home/<user>) and the group work
# area (/gpfs/data/abl/home/<user>) are DIFFERENT directories with different inodes -- only some
# subtrees, such as install/, are shared via symlink. Using $HOME once pointed the container
# cache at an empty directory, which silently re-pulls all 26 images and looks like the cache
# "stopped working". Set GARS_ROOT explicitly (e.g. in ~/.bashrc) to the root that holds
# install/ -- there is deliberately no default, because any default is someone's home.
GARS_ROOT="${GARS_ROOT:?[gars-env] FATAL: set GARS_ROOT to the root holding install/ (see _references/environment.md)}"

# --- environments -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two, because nextflow and clawbio have conflicting c-ares constraints and cannot be solved
# together. See _references/environment.md.
GARS_BIO="${GARS_BIO:-$GARS_ROOT/install/miniconda_clean/envs/gars-bio}"   # clawbio, apptainer, squashfuse
GARS_NXF="${GARS_NXF:-$GARS_ROOT/install/miniconda_clean/envs/gars-nxf}"   # nextflow, openjdk 17

# Order matters. gars-nxf first so `java` resolves to its OpenJDK 17 rather than the system
# Java 1.8 — Nextflow locates Java via PATH, and refuses anything below 17.
export PATH="$GARS_NXF/bin:$GARS_BIO/bin:$PATH"
export JAVA_HOME="$GARS_NXF"

# --- caches -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared across projects: container images and the pinned pipeline are immutable and reusable.
export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="${APPTAINER_CACHEDIR:-$GARS_ROOT/.apptainer_cache}"
export NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR"
export NXF_HOME="${NXF_HOME:-$GARS_ROOT/.nextflow_gars}"
mkdir -p "$APPTAINER_CACHEDIR" "$NXF_HOME"

# --- resolved locations -------------------------------------------------------------------
export GARS_PY="$GARS_BIO/bin/python"

# The retired clawbio skills (decision 0029) are resolved for inspection only -- no sub-stage
# invokes them. The literal site-packages path embeds a Python version that changes on any
# environment rebuild, hence the runtime resolution. Empty if clawbio is absent; that is fine.
# `|| true` carries this file's own promise ("Empty if clawbio is absent; that is fine")
# through a caller's `set -e`: a failed command substitution in an assignment is FATAL under
# -e, and every generated submit.sh runs with -e. The cluster never saw it -- clawbio is
# always installed there; the first host without it (the demo's recording rig) died here
# silently, before the script's first echo.
GARS_SKILLS=$("$GARS_PY" -c "import clawbio, pathlib; print(pathlib.Path(clawbio.__file__).parent / 'skills')" 2>/dev/null || true)
export GARS_SKILLS

# GARS-authored wrappers, versioned in this workspace and ours to maintain (decision 0012).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The workspace's batch executor, as a setting rather than a spelling (decision 0039).

GARS submits real work to a managed scheduler and never runs it in the current process
(decision 0027). That ruling is scheduler-agnostic; only its spelling was Slurm-coupled --
`sbatch` lived in generated bytes and in contract prose, so a site without Slurm could not
run GARS at all.

This module is the one door. It reads `_config/executor.yaml` from the project and answers
three questions:

    header(...)          the directives block a generated submit.sh opens with
    submit(script)       the argv that hands that script to the scheduler -> a job id
    status(job_id)       the argv that asks after it -> PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETED | FAILED

No descriptor file, or `name: slurm`, means the built-in Slurm descriptor, whose bytes are
identical to what this system generated before the seam existed (pinned by a golden-bytes
test). A cluster that upgrades GARS notices nothing.

The built-in `local` backend runs the generated script under `nohup`-style detachment and
reports the PID as the job id. It exists so the deterministic core can exercise a real
submit -> status -> completion walk with no cluster at all; it is POSIX-only, like every
other assumption this system already makes, and it is NOT a venue for analyses -- stage 03's
venue gate is unchanged.

Runs on stock python 3.6.8, stdlib only, like every `_system/` helper.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

EXIT_OK, EXIT_FAILURE, EXIT_REFUSED, EXIT_USAGE = 0, 1, 2, 3

#: The closed state vocabulary every backend maps onto. A caller polls until it sees a
#: terminal state; nothing else is a legal answer.
STATES = ("PENDING", "RUNNING", "COMPLETED", "FAILED")

#: The placeholders a `directives` line may name. Anything else is a descriptor error, said
#: by name rather than raised as a KeyError from inside a format string.
HEADER_FIELDS = ("project", "assay", "substage", "partition", "time", "cpus", "mem")

DESCRIPTOR_NAME = "executor.yaml"

#: Where the `local` backend keeps what it needs to answer `status` for a PID it started.
LOCAL_JOBS_DIR = ".gars_local_jobs"

SLURM = {
    "name": "slurm",
    "directives": [
        "#SBATCH --job-name={project}-{assay}",
        "#SBATCH --partition={partition}",
        "#SBATCH --time={time}",
        "#SBATCH --cpus-per-task={cpus}",
        "#SBATCH --mem={mem}",
        "#SBATCH --output={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.out",
        "#SBATCH --error={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.err",
    ],
    "submit_argv": ["sbatch", "{script}"],
    "job_id_regex": r"Submitted batch job (\d+)",
    "status_argv": ["sacct", "-j", "{job_id}", "--format=State", "--noheader"],
    "status_map": {
        "PENDING": "PENDING", "CONFIGURING": "PENDING", "REQUEUED": "PENDING",
        "SUSPENDED": "PENDING", "PREEMPTED": "PENDING",
        "RUNNING": "RUNNING", "COMPLETING": "RUNNING", "RESIZING": "RUNNING",
        "COMPLETED": "COMPLETED",
        "FAILED": "FAILED", "CANCELLED": "FAILED", "TIMEOUT": "FAILED",
        "NODE_FAIL": "FAILED", "OUT_OF_MEMORY": "FAILED", "BOOT_FAIL": "FAILED",
        "DEADLINE": "FAILED", "REVOKED": "FAILED",
    },
    "nextflow_config": "nextflow.slurm.config",
    #: The -profile the generated submit body passes to nextflow. A container runtime is a
    #: property of the venue, not of the science: this cluster runs apptainer; AWS Batch
    #: supplies each process's container itself and wants no profile at all (empty = omit).
    "nextflow_profile": "apptainer",
    "submit_note": "Slurm snapshots this script at submission: editing it never affects a "
                   "queued job.",
}

LOCAL = {
    "name": "local",
    "directives": [
        "# Executor: local. No scheduler directives -- this script is run directly, detached.",
        "# compute.* stays in the record: partition={partition} time={time} "
        "cpus={cpus} mem={mem}",
    ],
    "submit_argv": [],          # the local backend submits in-process, not through an argv
    "job_id_regex": "",
    "status_argv": [],
    "status_map": {},
    "nextflow_config": "",
    "nextflow_profile": "",
    "submit_note": "This script is run directly on this machine; editing it mid-run is a "
                   "race you will lose.",
}

# The workspace's batch executor (decision 0039). Seeded by stage 00; edit it per site.
#
# Required, not optional in spirit: GARS submits real work to a managed scheduler and never
# runs it in the current process (decision 0027). This file says WHICH scheduler. Delete it
# and the built-in Slurm descriptor below is what you get, byte for byte -- so an existing
# cluster workspace behaves exactly as it always has.
#
# The shape is deliberately narrow -- scalars, one-level lists, one-level `key: value` maps.
# `_system/` is stdlib-only (decision 0011), so this is parsed by a small parser we own, not
# by a YAML library. Do not reach for anchors, multi-line scalars or nested lists.
#
# Three doors, and nothing else:
#   header   the directives block the generated submit.sh opens with
#   submit   the argv that hands that GENERATED script to the scheduler -> a job id
#   status   the argv that asks after it -> PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETED | FAILED
#
# `submit_argv` runs the generated `submit.sh` and nothing else. It is not a place to add
# pipeline parameters, environment or wrapper logic: the audited parameter surface is
# `_config/<assay>.yaml`, and bypassing it is the one thing this file must never enable.

# The backend. `slurm` and `local` are built in; any other name means this file supplies the
# whole descriptor. (`local` runs the script detached on this machine and reports its PID --
# it is for testing the submit->status walk without a cluster, never a venue for analyses.)
name: slurm

# The directives block. Available placeholders, and only these:
#   {project} {assay} {substage} {partition} {time} {cpus} {mem}
# compute.partition / time / cpus / mem come from `_config/<assay>.yaml`.
directives:
  - "#SBATCH --job-name={project}-{assay}"
  - "#SBATCH --partition={partition}"
  - "#SBATCH --time={time}"
  - "#SBATCH --cpus-per-task={cpus}"
  - "#SBATCH --mem={mem}"
  - "#SBATCH --output={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.out"
  - "#SBATCH --error={substage}/logs/slurm-%j.err"

# How a script becomes a job. {script} is the generated submit.sh; it must appear.
submit_argv:
  - sbatch
  - "{script}"

# How the job id is read back out of what submit printed. First capture group wins.
# A quoted value is taken verbatim -- there is no escape processing, so a regex is
# written exactly as a regex, single backslashes and all.
job_id_regex: "Submitted batch job (\d+)"

# How the job is asked after. {job_id} must appear.
status_argv:
  - sacct
  - -j
  - "{job_id}"
  - --format=State
  - --noheader

# This backend's states, mapped onto the closed vocabulary. Closed means closed: a state that
# is not listed here is refused by name rather than guessed at, so an unfamiliar scheduler
# state can never be silently read as success.
status_map:
  PENDING: PENDING

# Project configuration schema

`projects/<project_title>/_config/` holds the scientific decisions for one project. **Stage 00
seeds it** from `_templates/config/` at project creation ([decision 0019]): every derivable
value filled, every scientific decision marked `<REQUIRED>`. **Stage 02 completes the
`<REQUIRED>` keys from menus** the user answers ([decision 0020]) — the genome registry, the
per-assay decision menu — and shows the result for confirmation before writing. No stage ever
chooses a scientific value silently, because a wrong value here produces confident, wrong
biology rather than an error, which is the one failure mode no downstream check can catch.

| File | Seeded by | Completed by | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<Assay ID>.yaml`, one per assay | stage 00, from `_templates/config/` | stage 02 menus (`_system/configure.py apply`), user confirms | stage 01 (assay-specific keys), the stage 02 wrapper |
| `nextflow.slurm.config` | stage 00, verbatim copy | nothing — edit by hand only if your allocation differs | every wrapper's generated `submit.sh` |

## The common shape

Every `<Assay ID>.yaml` has a `reference` block, a `compute` block, and at most one
assay-specific decision block. Values the genome menu sets travel together so they cannot be
mismatched (`_references/genomes.md`): fasta, gtf, and — where the assay uses them —
`mito_name`, `macs_gsize`, and the version-keyed `derived_dir`.

**`reference.genome` (the iGenomes key) is deliberately not supported.** The iGenomes GRCh38 is
the NCBI build with no `gene_biotype`; it killed a full run *after* counts were written
(decision 0005, failure 5). Every wrapper refuses the key; the registry's fasta+gtf pairs are
the verified route.

**`compute.*`** is infrastructure, not science: Slurm directives for the generated `submit.sh`
(`partition`, `time`, `cpus`, `mem`) plus `compute.work_dir` — Nextflow's scratch, **never
inside the project**: `work/` retains every process output so `-resume` can reuse it, and a
single run accumulates hundreds of GB there. `results/` is published with mode `copy`, so
`work/` is disposable once a run succeeds.

## Per-assay decision blocks

| Assay | Beyond `reference` + `compute` | Decision menu at stage 02 |
|---|---|---|
| `rnaseq_bulk` | `strandedness` (stage 01 reads it into the samplesheet); `de.formula`, `de.contrast` | genome + contrast (+ formula, default `~ condition`) |
| `atacseq_bulk` | `peaks.type` (narrow\|broad), `peaks.macs_gsize`, `reference.mito_name`, optional `reference.blacklist` | genome + peak type |
| `chipseq_bulk` | `peaks.type`, `peaks.macs_gsize`, optional `reference.blacklist` (no `mito_name` — the pipeline has no such parameter) | genome + peak type |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Differential accessibility, condition b vs a, over the ATAC-seq consensus peak set.

Run under gars-bio (pydeseq2==0.5.4). Reads the nf-core/atacseq featureCounts matrix and the
project design table; writes one results TSV. Never modifies its inputs.
"""

import argparse

import pandas as pd
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataSet
from pydeseq2.ds import DeseqStats


def load_counts(counts_path):
    counts = pd.read_csv(counts_path, sep="\t", skiprows=1)
    coords = counts.set_index("Geneid")[["Chr", "Start", "End"]]
    sample_cols = [c for c in counts.columns
                   if c not in ("Geneid", "Chr", "Start", "End", "Strand", "Length")]
    matrix = counts.set_index("Geneid")[sample_cols]
    return matrix, coords


def load_design(design_path, sample_cols):
    design = pd.read_csv(design_path)
    # featureCounts names columns after the BAM files it was given (<sample_id>_REPn...);
    # map each count column back to its design row by the sample_id prefix.
    id_by_col = {}
    for col in sample_cols:
        matches = [sid for sid in design["sample_id"] if col.startswith(sid.rsplit("-r", 1)[0])]
        hits = [sid for sid in design["sample_id"]
                if col.lower().replace("_rep", "-r").startswith(sid.lower())]
        id_by_col[col] = hits[0] if hits else matches[0]
    meta = design.set_index("sample_id").loc[[id_by_col[c] for c in sample_cols]]
    meta.index = sample_cols
    meta.index.name = "sample"
    return meta[["condition"]]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--counts", required=True, help="consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.featureCounts.txt")
    ap.add_argument("--design", required=True, help="atacseq_bulk_design.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output TSV path")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    matrix, coords = load_counts(args.counts)
    meta = load_design(args.design, list(matrix.columns))

    counts_t = matrix.T  # DeseqDataSet wants samples x features
    counts_t.index.name = "sample"

    dds = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts_t, metadata=meta, design_factors="condition",
                        ref_level=["condition", "a"], refit_cooks=True)
    dds.deseq2()

    stats = DeseqStats(dds, contrast=["condition", "b", "a"])
    stats.summary()

    results = stats.results_df.join(coords)
    results = results[["Chr", "Start", "End", "baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE",
                        "stat", "pvalue", "padj"]]
    results.index.name = "peak_id"
    results = results.sort_values("padj")
    results.to_csv(args.out, sep="\t")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import argparse
import re

import pandas as pd
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataSet
from pydeseq2.ds import DeseqStats

# nf-core/atacseq names featureCounts columns after the BAMs it was given:
# "<group>_REP<replicate>.mLb.clN.sorted.bam" -- matched back to the design table's own
# group/replicate columns rather than parsed further, since that pairing is the design's job.
COLUMN_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<group>.+)_REP(?P<replicate>\d+)\.")


def load_counts(counts_path):
    counts = pd.read_csv(counts_path, sep="\t", skiprows=1)
    coords = counts.set_index("Geneid")[["Chr", "Start", "End"]]
    sample_cols = [c for c in counts.columns
                   if c not in ("Geneid", "Chr", "Start", "End", "Strand", "Length")]
    matrix = counts.set_index("Geneid")[sample_cols]
    return matrix, coords


def load_design(design_path, sample_cols):
    design = pd.read_csv(design_path)
    design["replicate"] = design["replicate"].astype(str)
    rows = []
    for col in sample_cols:
        m = COLUMN_RE.match(col)
        if not m:
            raise ValueError("count column %r does not match <group>_REP<n>." % col)
        match = design[(design["group"] == m.group("group"))
                        & (design["replicate"] == m.group("replicate"))]
        if len(match) != 1:
            raise ValueError("count column %r matched %d design rows, expected 1"
                              % (col, len(match)))
        rows.append(match.iloc[0])
    meta = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    meta.index = sample_cols
    meta.index.name = "sample"
    return meta[["condition"]]

"""

import argparse

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataSet

from importlib import import_module

_diffacc = import_module("01_differential_accessibility".replace("-", "_")) \
    if False else None  # placeholder, unused -- kept import-free below

PADJ_CUT = 0.05


def ma_plot(results, out_path):
    sig = results["padj"] < PADJ_CUT
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
    ax.scatter(results.loc[~sig, "baseMean"], results.loc[~sig, "log2FoldChange"],
               s=8, color="#888888", alpha=0.5, label="padj >= 0.05")
    ax.scatter(results.loc[sig, "baseMean"], results.loc[sig, "log2FoldChange"],
               s=10, color="#d62728", alpha=0.8, label="padj < 0.05")
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_xlabel("Mean of normalised counts")
    ax.set_ylabel("log2 fold change (b vs a)")
    ax.set_title("MA plot: condition b vs a")
    ax.legend(frameon=False)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def volcano_plot(results, out_path):
    sig = results["padj"] < PADJ_CUT
    neg_log_padj = -np.log10(results["padj"].clip(lower=1e-300))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
    ax.scatter(results.loc[~sig, "log2FoldChange"], neg_log_padj[~sig],
               s=8, color="#888888", alpha=0.5, label="padj >= 0.05")
    ax.scatter(results.loc[sig, "log2FoldChange"], neg_log_padj[sig],
               s=10, color="#d62728", alpha=0.8, label="padj < 0.05")
    ax.axhline(-np.log10(PADJ_CUT), color="black", linewidth=0.8, linestyle="--")
    ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold change (b vs a)")
    ax.set_ylabel("-log10(padj)")
    ax.set_title("Volcano plot: condition b vs a")
    ax.legend(frameon=False)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def pca_plot(counts_path, design_path, out_path):

    spec = import_util.spec_from_file_location(
        "diffacc", __file__.replace("02_plot_results.py", "01_differential_accessibility.py"))
    diffacc = import_util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(diffacc)

    matrix, _ = diffacc.load_counts(counts_path)
    meta = diffacc.load_design(design_path, list(matrix.columns))
    counts_t = matrix.T
    counts_t.index.name = "sample"

    dds = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts_t, metadata=meta, design_factors="condition",
                        ref_level=["condition", "a"])
    dds.deseq2()
    dds.vst()
    vst_counts = pd.DataFrame(dds.layers["vst_counts"], index=dds.obs_names,
                               columns=dds.var_names)

    from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
    pca = PCA(n_components=2)
    coords = pca.fit_transform(vst_counts.values)
    pca_df = pd.DataFrame(coords, columns=["PC1", "PC2"], index=vst_counts.index)
    pca_df["condition"] = meta.loc[pca_df.index, "condition"].values

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
    sns.scatterplot(data=pca_df, x="PC1", y="PC2", hue="condition", s=100, ax=ax)
    for sample, row in pca_df.iterrows():
        ax.annotate(sample, (row["PC1"], row["PC2"]), fontsize=7, xytext=(3, 3),
                    textcoords="offset points")
    var_pct = pca.explained_variance_ratio_ * 100
    ax.set_xlabel("PC1 (%.1f%%)" % var_pct[0])
    ax.set_ylabel("PC2 (%.1f%%)" % var_pct[1])
    ax.set_title("PCA of variance-stabilised peak counts")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--results", required=True, help="differential_accessibility.tsv")
    ap.add_argument("--counts", required=True, help="consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.featureCounts.txt")
    ap.add_argument("--design", required=True, help="atacseq_bulk_design.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--ma-out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--volcano-out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--pca-out", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    results = pd.read_csv(args.results, sep="\t", index_col="peak_id")
    ma_plot(results, args.ma_out)
    volcano_plot(results, args.volcano_out)
    pca_plot(args.counts, args.design, args.pca_out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Differential accessibility, condition b vs a, over the ATAC-seq consensus peak set.

Run under gars-bio (pydeseq2==0.5.4). Reads the nf-core/atacseq featureCounts matrix and the
project design table; writes one results TSV. Never modifies its inputs.
"""

import argparse
import re

import pandas as pd
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataSet
from pydeseq2.ds import DeseqStats

# nf-core/atacseq names featureCounts columns after the BAMs it was given:
# "<group>_REP<replicate>.mLb.clN.sorted.bam" -- matched back to the design table's own
# group/replicate columns rather than parsed further, since that pairing is the design's job.
COLUMN_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<group>.+)_REP(?P<replicate>\d+)\.")


def load_counts(counts_path):
    counts = pd.read_csv(counts_path, sep="\t", skiprows=1)
    coords = counts.set_index("Geneid")[["Chr", "Start", "End"]]
    sample_cols = [c for c in counts.columns
                   if c not in ("Geneid", "Chr", "Start", "End", "Strand", "Length")]
    matrix = counts.set_index("Geneid")[sample_cols]
    return matrix, coords


def load_design(design_path, sample_cols):
    design = pd.read_csv(design_path)
    design["replicate"] = design["replicate"].astype(str)
    rows = []
    for col in sample_cols:
        m = COLUMN_RE.match(col)
        if not m:
            raise ValueError("count column %r does not match <group>_REP<n>." % col)
        match = design[(design["group"] == m.group("group"))
                        & (design["replicate"] == m.group("replicate"))]
        if len(match) != 1:
            raise ValueError("count column %r matched %d design rows, expected 1"
                              % (col, len(match)))
        rows.append(match.iloc[0])
    meta = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    meta.index = sample_cols
    meta.index.name = "sample"
    return meta[["condition"]]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--counts", required=True, help="consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.featureCounts.txt")
    ap.add_argument("--design", required=True, help="atacseq_bulk_design.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output TSV path")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    matrix, coords = load_counts(args.counts)
    meta = load_design(args.design, list(matrix.columns))

    counts_t = matrix.T  # DeseqDataSet wants samples x features
    counts_t.index.name = "sample"

    dds = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts_t, metadata=meta, design_factors="condition",
                        ref_level=["condition", "a"], refit_cooks=True)
    dds.deseq2()

    stats = DeseqStats(dds, contrast=["condition", "b", "a"])
    stats.summary()

    results = stats.results_df.join(coords)
    results = results[["Chr", "Start", "End", "baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE",
                        "stat", "pvalue", "padj"]]
    results.index.name = "peak_id"
    results = results.sort_values("padj")
    results.to_csv(args.out, sep="\t")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Differential accessibility, condition b vs a, over the ATAC-seq consensus peak set.

Run under gars-bio (pydeseq2==0.5.4). Reads the nf-core/atacseq featureCounts matrix and the
project design table; writes one results TSV. Never modifies its inputs.
"""

import argparse
import re

import pandas as pd
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataSet
from pydeseq2.ds import DeseqStats

# nf-core/atacseq names featureCounts columns after the BAMs it was given:
# "<group>_REP<replicate>.mLb.clN.sorted.bam" -- matched back to the design table's own
# group/replicate columns rather than parsed further, since that pairing is the design's job.
COLUMN_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<group>.+)_REP(?P<replicate>\d+)\.")


def load_counts(counts_path):
    counts = pd.read_csv(counts_path, sep="\t", skiprows=1)
    sample_cols = [c for c in counts.columns
                   if c not in ("Geneid", "Chr", "Start", "End", "Strand", "Length")]
    matrix = counts.set_index("Geneid")[sample_cols]
    return matrix


def load_coords(consensus_bed_path):
    bed = pd.read_csv(consensus_bed_path, sep="\t", header=None,
                       names=["Chr", "Start", "End", "Geneid", "score", "strand"])
    return bed.set_index("Geneid")[["Chr", "Start", "End"]]


def load_design(design_path, sample_cols):
    design = pd.read_csv(design_path)
    design["replicate"] = design["replicate"].astype(str)
    rows = []
    for col in sample_cols:
        m = COLUMN_RE.match(col)
        if not m:
            raise ValueError("count column %r does not match <group>_REP<n>." % col)
        match = design[(design["group"] == m.group("group"))
                        & (design["replicate"] == m.group("replicate"))]
        if len(match) != 1:
            raise ValueError("count column %r matched %d design rows, expected 1"
                              % (col, len(match)))
        rows.append(match.iloc[0])
    meta = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    meta.index = sample_cols
    meta.index.name = "sample"
    return meta[["condition"]]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--counts", required=True, help="consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.featureCounts.txt")
    ap.add_argument("--design", required=True, help="atacseq_bulk_design.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output TSV path")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    matrix, coords = load_counts(args.counts)
    meta = load_design(args.design, list(matrix.columns))

    counts_t = matrix.T  # DeseqDataSet wants samples x features
    counts_t.index.name = "sample"

    dds = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts_t, metadata=meta, design_factors="condition",
                        ref_level=["condition", "a"], refit_cooks=True)
    dds.deseq2()

    stats = DeseqStats(dds, contrast=["condition", "b", "a"])
    stats.summary()

    results = stats.results_df.join(coords)
    results = results[["Chr", "Start", "End", "baseMean", "log2FoldChange", "lfcSE",
                        "stat", "pvalue", "padj"]]
    results.index.name = "peak_id"
    results = results.sort_values("padj")
    results.to_csv(args.out, sep="\t")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""MA, volcano and PCA plots for the condition b vs a differential accessibility results.

Run under gars-bio (matplotlib, seaborn, pydeseq2). Reads the results TSV written by
01_differential_accessibility.py plus the same counts/design inputs for the PCA plot; never
modifies its inputs.
"""

import argparse

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
from pydeseq2.dds import DeseqDataSet

PADJ_CUT = 0.05


def ma_plot(results, out_path):
    sig = results["padj"] < PADJ_CUT
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
    ax.scatter(results.loc[~sig, "baseMean"], results.loc[~sig, "log2FoldChange"],
               s=8, color="#888888", alpha=0.5, label="padj >= 0.05")
    ax.scatter(results.loc[sig, "baseMean"], results.loc[sig, "log2FoldChange"],
               s=10, color="#d62728", alpha=0.8, label="padj < 0.05")
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_xlabel("Mean of normalised counts")
    ax.set_ylabel("log2 fold change (b vs a)")
    ax.set_title("MA plot: condition b vs a")
    ax.legend(frameon=False)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def volcano_plot(results, out_path):
    sig = results["padj"] < PADJ_CUT
    neg_log_padj = -np.log10(results["padj"].clip(lower=1e-300))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
    ax.scatter(results.loc[~sig, "log2FoldChange"], neg_log_padj[~sig],
               s=8, color="#888888", alpha=0.5, label="padj >= 0.05")
    ax.scatter(results.loc[sig, "log2FoldChange"], neg_log_padj[sig],
               s=10, color="#d62728", alpha=0.8, label="padj < 0.05")
    ax.axhline(-np.log10(PADJ_CUT), color="black", linewidth=0.8, linestyle="--")
    ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold change (b vs a)")
    ax.set_ylabel("-log10(padj)")
    ax.set_title("Volcano plot: condition b vs a")
    ax.legend(frameon=False)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def pca_plot(counts_path, design_path, out_path):
    from importlib import util as import_util
    spec = import_util.spec_from_file_location(
        "diffacc", __file__.replace("02_plot_results.py", "01_differential_accessibility.py"))
    diffacc = import_util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(diffacc)

    matrix, _ = diffacc.load_counts(counts_path)
    meta = diffacc.load_design(design_path, list(matrix.columns))
    counts_t = matrix.T
    counts_t.index.name = "sample"

    dds = DeseqDataSet(counts=counts_t, metadata=meta, design_factors="condition",
                        ref_level=["condition", "a"])
    dds.deseq2()
    dds.vst()
    vst_counts = pd.DataFrame(dds.layers["vst_counts"], index=dds.obs_names,
                               columns=dds.var_names)

    from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
    pca = PCA(n_components=2)
    coords = pca.fit_transform(vst_counts.values)
    pca_df = pd.DataFrame(coords, columns=["PC1", "PC2"], index=vst_counts.index)
    pca_df["condition"] = meta.loc[pca_df.index, "condition"].values

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))
    sns.scatterplot(data=pca_df, x="PC1", y="PC2", hue="condition", s=100, ax=ax)
    for sample, row in pca_df.iterrows():
        ax.annotate(sample, (row["PC1"], row["PC2"]), fontsize=7, xytext=(3, 3),
                    textcoords="offset points")
    var_pct = pca.explained_variance_ratio_ * 100
    ax.set_xlabel("PC1 (%.1f%%)" % var_pct[0])
    ax.set_ylabel("PC2 (%.1f%%)" % var_pct[1])
    ax.set_title("PCA of variance-stabilised peak counts")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--results", required=True, help="differential_accessibility.tsv")
    ap.add_argument("--counts", required=True, help="consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.featureCounts.txt")
    ap.add_argument("--design", required=True, help="atacseq_bulk_design.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--ma-out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--volcano-out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--pca-out", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    results = pd.read_csv(args.results, sep="\t", index_col="peak_id")
    ma_plot(results, args.ma_out)
    volcano_plot(results, args.volcano_out)
    pca_plot(args.counts, args.design, args.pca_out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def cmd_verify(args, workspace):
    result = {"command": "verify", "ok": False, "analysis": args.analysis,
              "missing": [], "empty": []}
    project = Path(args.project)
    adir = find_analysis(project, args.analysis)
    if adir is None:
        result["error"] = "no analysis %r under %s" % (args.analysis, stage_root(project))
        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)
    text = (adir / "PLAN.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    m = re.search(r"^Status: APPROVED( .*)?$", text, re.M)
    if not m:
        result["error"] = ("PLAN.md is not approved; the analysis must not have run. If it "
                           "did, that is the failure to report -- do not approve after the "
                           "fact.")
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)
    holds, why = approval_holds(adir / "PLAN.md", adir / APPROVAL_RECORD)
    if not holds:
        result["error"] = ("PLAN.md is not approved: %s. A `Status: APPROVED` line is an approval "
                           "only when `approve` wrote it together with its record, and a plan "
                           "edited after approval is a new analysis -- run `create` again. If "
                           "the analysis already ran, that is the failure to report (decision "
                           "0042)." % why)
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)

    outputs = parse_outputs_table(text)
    if not outputs:
        result["error"] = "the approved plan declares no outputs; nothing to verify"
        return emit(result, EXIT_FAILURE)

    for fname, ftype, _ in outputs:
        p = adir / fname
        if not p.is_file():
            result["missing"].append(fname)
        elif p.stat().st_size == 0:
            result["empty"].append(fname)
    if result["missing"] or result["empty"]:
        return emit(result, EXIT_FAILURE)

    with ws.atomic_open(adir / "OUTPUTS.tsv") as fh:
        fh.write("# type\trole\tpath\n")
        for fname, ftype, _ in outputs:
            fh.write("%s\tnative\t%s\n" % (ftype, fname))

    now = datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
    with ws.atomic_open(adir / "STATUS") as fh:
        fh.write("COMPLETE %s\n" % now)

    version = ws.template_version(workspace)
    model = args.model or "unknown"
    goal = re.search(r"^## Goal\n(.*?)(?=^## |\Z)", text, re.S | re.M)
    goal_line = " ".join(goal.group(1).split()) if goal else ""
    if len(goal_line) > 200:
        # break at a word, not mid-word -- this line is read by humans in HISTORY.md
        goal_line = goal_line[:200].rsplit(" ", 1)[0] + " ..."
    entry = "\n".join([
        "## <ISO-8601 date> — 03_custom_analysis/%s — analysis complete" % args.analysis,
        "",
        "Template version: %s" % version,
        "Model: %s" % model,
        "Plan: %s/%s/PLAN.md (approved%s)" % (STAGE_DIR, args.analysis, m.group(1) or ""),
        "Goal: %s" % goal_line,
        "Outputs: " + ", ".join("`%s` (%s)" % (f, t) for f, t, _ in outputs),
    ])
    result.update({"ok": True, "outputs": [{"path": f, "type": t} for f, t, _ in outputs],
                   "template_version": version, "model": model, "history_entry": entry})
    return emit(result, EXIT_OK)


# --- main --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--workspace", type=Path, default=None)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd")

    c = sub.add_parser("create", help="allocate an analysis directory with a PLAN.md skeleton")
    c.add_argument("--project", required=True)
    c.add_argument("--slug", required=True, help="short kebab-case name for the analysis")
